text:
samir: Quick heads-up — I'm starting onboarding for Boreal-12B (from community release). model card attached in the repo. primary concern: license looks like a custom CC-style with a commercial restriction and an attribution clause. planning to run int8/ql4 quant and push a quantized artifact to our internal model registry. any red flags?

nina: do you have the exact license text? can you paste the clause that mentions hosting/redistribution?

samir: here's the excerpt from model_card.md: "Model and weights are provided under the Boreal NonCommercial Attribution License v1.0: no commercial use, redistribution allowed for research/education with attribution; derived weight artifacts (including quantized binaries) must include original checksum and attribution notice."

omar: interesting. so they explicitly mention derived weight artifacts. that sounds like we can keep a quantized internal copy, but external hosting or offering via hosted API might be prohibited. we should confirm what they mean by commercial (does internal product usage count?).

melissa: tagging legal: @melissa. from the excerpt it reads like a non-commercial license. typical interpretation: use in a revenue-generating product or offering a paid API would be commercial. internal R&D or evaluation usually OK. redistribution clause is the sticky part — they require attribution and checksum in redistributed artifacts. also need to check whether the license has a sublicensing clause.

legal-bot: automated note: please attach link to upstream license URL and the model SHA256 for provenance checks. recommended next step: open a Legal intake ticket with intended usage (hosted API? internal-only?).

samir: link: https://models.example/boreal-12b/model_card.md SHA256: 3f2a9b...f9c. plan is: 1) run q4_0 quant locally, 2) add artifact to internal-registry (private), 3) use it from Redwood Dedicated test pool (customer sandbox) for performance evals — not production-hosted.

ken: small flag: customer sandboxes might still be considered commercial if the customer pays for the environment. melissa, is a sandbox used for paid PoCs considered commercial?

melissa: good point. if the sandbox is part of a paid service or used to provide paid support, it could be commercial. If it's purely internal evaluation with no paid access, it's likely non-commercial. we need the intake ticket details to be sure. also, the checksum/attribution requirement means any derived weight export we hand to customers (even q4 binaries) must carry the notice.

nina: on the quant side — is there any wording about allowed transforms (e.g., pruning, quant)? some licenses forbid creating derivatives that change model behavior. I scanned the card, it mentions "derived artifacts" but no explicit ban on quantization. still ambiguous.

omar: from a risk perspective: two safe options: A) keep quantized weights strictly in private registries and internal infra and forbid sharing with customers; B) reach out to upstream to request an explicit redistribution exception for quantized/opt artifacts (we can offer attribution + checksum). option B might take time.

samir: technical note — my quant command (for reproducibility):

```bash
rwi quantize --model boreal-12b --target q4_0 --seed 42 --out ./artifacts/boreal-12b-q4_0
sha256sum ./artifacts/boreal-12b-q4_0 > ./artifacts/README_checksum.txt
```

samir: I'll include the SHA and attribution text in the registry metadata per the license if Legal signs off.

melissa: please file the Legal intake with the exact usage: "Dedicated test pool for customer sandbox (paid)" vs "internal-only evaluation". if it's the former, we probably need a commercial license or an explicit exception. if the latter, we can proceed but must keep artifacts private and track provenance.

ken: also add a note about telemetry — if we log customer prompts or outputs to eval quality, ensure that doesn't count as offering the model.

samir: thanks — I'll open the intake with details and mark the onboarding PR as blocked until we get clearance. in the meantime, I'll run the quant evals on an isolated internal bucket and keep artifacts private. will update thread with ticket link. :thumbsup:
